title: Conspiracy Thinking, Online Misinformation, and Hate: Insights from an Italian News Story Using Topic Modeling Techniques
screen_reason: Topic-modelling study of 35,055 + 1,815,602 Italian tweets around the release of aid worker Silvia Romano (May-June 2020). It is largely unsupervised modelling work (normally excluded), but it does report one observed share with an explicit denominator that speaks to misinformation spreading: 'about 23% of these 653 users mentioned words in topics related to rumors and conspiracy theories concerning Bill Gates or racial hoaxes'. That is a share of users posting misinformation-related content from platform data, so one SHARING (actor_share) row is extracted - flagged borderline, low confidence and within_misinfo_content because the denominator is itself a conspiracy-selected subsample and the labelling is an unvalidated topic model.

estimates.country: Italy (tweets filtered for the Italian language)
estimates.measure_type: % of the authors of the most controversial tweets about Silvia Romano's release whose subsequent tweets used words from topics related to rumours and conspiracy theories (Bill Gates, racial hoaxes)
estimates.denominator: 653 Twitter users who authored the tweets assigned (probability > 0.5) to the most polemical 'controversies' topic about Silvia Romano's release, drawn from the 18,235 users who tweeted about her release
estimates.definition: User's aggregated subsequent tweets (dataset D3, 216,247 tweets) contained words belonging to LDA-U topics that the author labelled as rumours/conspiracy theories about Bill Gates or as racial hoaxes about immigrants
estimates.misinfo_def: "This topic embraced some rumors and conspiracy theories related to the COVID-19 pandemic that were proliferated given the lack of scientific consensus on the virus's spread" (no formal definition; the author concedes "There is a lack of academic consensus on how to measure these concepts (canceled accounts are by no means a proxy for misinformation)")
estimates.source_quote: 23% of these 653 users mentioned words in topics related to rumors and conspiracy theories concerning Bill Gates or racial hoaxes.
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Unsupervised topic models only: biterm topic model (BTM) on D1 to select the 'controversies' topic, then LDA-U on user-aggregated tweets (30 topics) in D3; topics labelled by the single author, guided by Mimno coherence scores computed against an ad hoc three-book Italian corpus. No fact-checking, no external ground truth, no human validation of individual tweets, no inter-coder reliability.
estimates.moderator_quote: The first dataset, denoted by D1, was built on all the tweets in Italian containing the keywords "Silvia Romano" ... D3 consisted of 216,247 tweets, which were aggregated by 653 users. These were the authors of the aforementioned most controversial posts on the release of Silvia Romano.
estimates.notes: JUDGEMENT CALL FOR THE ADJUDICATOR: an EXCLUDE decision is also defensible (this is unsupervised modelling work and the number is approximate, 'about 23%'). I kept it because a share of users observed to post misinformation-related content, with a stated denominator, meets the SHARING criterion. It must NOT enter any prevalence pool: the denominator is a conspiracy-selected subsample (users chosen because they wrote the most polemical tweets about one news story), which is why within_misinfo_content=true; and the numerator is topic-model word membership, not verified false content. topic=other because the two misinformation strands are mixed (COVID-19 Bill Gates conspiracy + immigration 'racial hoaxes') on top of a general-news seed event. denom_scope=topical + denom_selection=curated (a topic-truncated subset of a single-issue keyword corpus).

missed_or_uncertain: (1) '207 (about 31.7%) used the more offensive words contained in Topic T3' - offensive/toxic language, i.e. hate speech, not misinformation, so no row (the paper itself keeps the two constructs separate and finds no strict relationship between them). (2) Word-frequency counts ('costata' 328 and 'terrorista' 843 tweets out of 35,055; 'islamica' 285/35,055; trigram scores) are keyword occurrence, not a veracity classification. (3) Account/tweet survival figures two years later (15,542/18,235 = 82.4% of users remained; 222/271 = 81.9%; 44,539/61,815 = 70%; 24,185/61,815 = 39.1%; 'only around 20% of them were unavailable') are moderation/attrition measures - the author explicitly warns 'canceled accounts are by no means a proxy for misinformation'. (4) 271 users / 61,815 tweets assigned to the misinformation-and-hate topic set T is a bare count of accounts with no matching share of activity, so it cannot be turned into a CONCENTRATION row (R1 requires both conc_group_pct and conc_share_pct); the activity comparison given (mean 228.1 tweets per user in D4 vs 118.1 in D2\D4) is a per-user intensity of ALL tweeting, not of misinformation. (5) No CONTENT share of tweets classified false is reported anywhere.

rob.design: Case-study Twitter analysis; frame = all Italian-language tweets containing 'Silvia Romano' via the Twitter streaming API 8-16 May 2020 (D1, 35,055 tweets, 18,235 users, retweets excluded upstream) plus all subsequent tweets by those users to 2 June 2020 (D2, 1,815,602); classification entirely by unsupervised topic models (BTM, LDA-U) with author-assigned labels and coherence scores from an ad hoc three-book corpus; single author, no inter-coder reliability, no validation against fact-checks; author notes the Italian-Twitter sample is not representative of Italian society.
rob.item6_quote: This topic embraced some rumors and conspiracy theories related to the COVID-19 pandemic that were proliferated given the lack of scientific consensus on the virus's spread.
rob.item10_quote: Out of a total of 653 users who posted the most controversial tweets on the release of Silvia Romano, 207 (about 31.7%) used the more offensive words contained in Topic T3^{D3,30}. Of course, these words were not necessarily directed to Silvia Romano. Furthermore, about 23% of these 653 users mentioned words in topics related to rumors and conspiracy theories concerning Bill Gates or racial hoaxes.
